name: BLINK
ability_definition: The ability to quickly and accurately compare similarities and differences among sets of letters, numbers, objects, pictures, or patterns. The things to be compared may be presented at the same time or one after the other. This ability also includes comparing a presented object with a remembered object.

task_realism.reasoning: Several BLINK subtasks require comparing images side by side to find sameness or difference: visual similarity, visual correspondence, forensics detection, jigsaw and multi-view matching. That is the core act of perceptual comparison. However, these are curated computer-vision probes, not workplace tasks. Real perceptual-speed work means checking invoice numbers against records, proofreading, verifying part labels, spotting defects on a line, or reconciling codes. Some subtasks, such as depth, reflectance and counting, do not involve comparison at all.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: The defining feature of this ability is speed under time pressure, and BLINK scores accuracy with no time limit. It is a static, untimed evaluation with no throughput demand, no fatigue, no sustained high-volume stream, and no consequences for errors. It measures whether a comparison can be made correctly, not whether it can be made quickly and repeatedly.

construct_coverage.reasoning: BLINK covers only the accuracy side of comparing objects, pictures and patterns shown at the same time. It omits speed entirely. It has no letter or number string comparison, which is central in clerical work, and it does not test comparison with a remembered or sequentially presented item. Non-comparison subtasks further dilute how well it targets this ability.

format_match.reasoning: The inputs are real photographs and image pairs, which is somewhat realistic. The outputs, however, are forced multiple-choice answers, often keyed to artificial overlay markers such as labeled points or boxes. Real work produces flagged discrepancies, pass/fail decisions or corrected records across large volumes of items. It does not produce a single choice among lettered options on a curated pair.

transferability_reasoning: BLINK partially captures the accuracy of visual side-by-side comparison, which is one component of Perceptual Speed. It misses the speed dimension that defines the ability. It also omits alphanumeric comparison and memory-based comparison, and it uses a multiple-choice format far from real inspection or verification work. High BLINK scores would indicate reliable visual matching judgments but say little about fast, high-volume comparison performance in the workplace.

2024.metric: accuracy (%) on the BLINK validation set, multiple choice
2024.human_reference: General adult workforce (people doing routine visual comparison and matching at work: inspection, clerical checking, data verification)

2025.human_reference: General adult population (Perceptual Speed is a basic perceptual-comparison ability used across ordinary work settings)

2026.human_reference: General adult population. Perceptual speed and visual comparison are basic abilities used across many jobs, and BLINK tasks were designed to be solvable by ordinary humans 'within a blink'.
